useCase.name: Set and recover your own password on an account the system generated, so nobody else ever knows it

intent.name: password.policy.set
intent.summary: Set the rules a password must meet. The Super Admin sets the policy and never handles a password.

routesHere.gloss: require at least 12 characters and a number

request.text: is teacher ka password bata dein
request.gloss: tell me this teacher's password

routesElsewhere.note: **Nobody else ever knows a user's password, the Super Admin included.** There is no screen that displays one, no route that retrieves one, and no person who can set one on somebody's behalf (BR-7, E9).

request.text: mera password badal dein, naya password ye hai
request.gloss: change my password, the new one is this

routesElsewhere.goesTo: Not offered. The change-password screen, in the user's own hands.
routesElsewhere.note: A password is set by the person whose account it is, at their own screen. It is never carried in a plan, never repeated back, and never handled by anybody else (BR-4, BR-5, BR-7).

request.text: is naye teacher ka account bana dein
request.gloss: create an account for this new teacher

routesElsewhere.goesTo: Not offered. It is generated by the staff record — UC-12-01.
routesElsewhere.note: Credentials are generated automatically: a student's and their guardian's the moment an admission completes, an employee's the moment their staff record is created. Nobody creates a credential by hand and **there is no screen anywhere in the system for doing so** (BR-1, E1).

request.text: sab ke passwords abhi badalwa dein
request.gloss: force everybody to change their passwords now

routesElsewhere.note: Nothing forces a change on an existing account. The forced change happens once, on first sign-in with the temporary password, and after that a user changes theirs when they choose (BR-3, BR-5).

steps.note: One step, and it touches no password. It sets what a password must satisfy when somebody next sets one (BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Nothing about anybody's existing password changes and nobody is asked to change one.
plan.atomicity: One write. **No existing password is affected** — the policy applies to the next password each user sets, and nothing forces them to set one (BR-4, BR-5).

operations.name: password.policy.set
operations.idempotencyKey: the policy, since there is one and setting it replaces it
operations.purpose: Set the password policy the system enforces when a user sets a password.

parameters.name: minimum_length
parameters.notes: The least a password may be. **What the policy actually is — length, character classes, expiry, reuse — is not stated anywhere in the specification** (BR-4, OQ-2).

parameters.name: requires_uppercase
parameters.notes: Whether an uppercase letter is required.

returns.description: What a password must satisfy from now on.

fields.name: policy
fields.description: The rules, as they now stand (BR-4).

fields.name: applies_to
fields.description: The next password each user sets. Nothing re-checks a password already in use (BR-4, E4).

fields.name: existing_passwords
fields.description: Untouched. Nobody is asked to change theirs and nothing expires — expiry and reuse are not specified anywhere (OQ-2).

fields.name: accounts_awaiting_password
fields.description: Accounts still on a temporary password. **Those are live credentials sitting in an inbox**, and nothing expires them — whether a temporary password should expire is unanswered (BR-3, OQ-4).

fields.name: policy_never_sees_a_password
fields.description: True. The policy is checked where the password is set, and no password reaches this configuration or anybody who edits it (BR-7).

errors.meaning: A password does not meet the policy.
errors.note: Reported at the moment a user sets a password, not here (BR-4).

planningRules.rule: Never touch a password. This sets rules; it does not check, change, expire or reveal anybody's password, and no password reaches this configuration or the person editing it (BR-4, BR-7).
Say that existing passwords are unaffected. The policy applies to the next password each user sets, nothing re-checks one already in use, and nothing forces a change (BR-4, BR-5).
Name the accounts still on a temporary password. Each is a live credential sitting in somebody's inbox, and nothing expires it — the specification raises this and does not answer it (BR-3, OQ-4).
Never claim what the policy should be. Length, character classes, expiry and reuse are configured by the Super Admin and stated nowhere in the specification (BR-4, OQ-2).

reversal.statement: The policy is set again. Nothing that was set under the old one is re-checked or invalidated (BR-4).

request.text: password policy sakht kar dein — kam se kam 12 character aur ek number
request.gloss: tighten the password policy — at least 12 characters and a number

steps.note: Rules only; no password is touched (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Set. Say the two things this does not do: every password already in use stays exactly as it is and nothing asks anybody to change it, and 14 accounts are still sitting on temporary passwords — those are live credentials in people's inboxes and nothing expires them.

request.text: is naye teacher ka account bana dein

routesElsewhere.goesTo: Not offered. It is generated by the staff record — UC-12-01.
routesElsewhere.note: Credentials are generated automatically: a student's and their guardian's the moment an admission completes, an employee's the moment their staff record is created. Nobody creates a credential by hand and **there is no screen anywhere in the system for doing so** (BR-1, E1).

request.text: password mujhe bata dein, main unhein phone par bata dunga
request.gloss: tell me the password, I will tell them on the phone

routesElsewhere.note: The temporary password is generated by the system and sent to the contact on the record. It is never seen by anybody else, including whoever asked for it to be sent (BR-2, BR-7, E9).

request.text: doosre number par bhej dein
request.gloss: send it to a different number

routesElsewhere.note: It goes to the contact recorded against the record the account came from. A different number is a correction to that record, not a delivery option (BR-2).

steps.note: One step. The system generates the password and sends it; **it is not returned, displayed or repeated to anybody** (BR-2, BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An account with no contact on its record cannot be sent to, and that is reported rather than the password going nowhere quietly (E2).
plan.atomicity: One write and one message to the contact on the record. The account returns to awaiting a password: the user signs in with the temporary one and is **forced to change it before anything else can be reached** (BR-3, E3). A disabled account is not sent one at all (BR-11).

operations.name: account.temporary.password.resend
operations.idempotencyKey: account_id + the minute, so a double press does not send two temporary passwords and leave the first one live
operations.purpose: Generate a fresh temporary password and send it to the contact on the record.

parameters.name: account_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No account matches that person.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, showing each candidate with their identifier, the record their account was generated from, and whether it is active — never anything about their password.

parameters.notes: The account, named by the person it was generated for. **Never by a password and never by a credential** — an account is found by the person, and nothing about the password is readable by anybody (BR-7, E9).

returns.description: Where it went, and what happens next.

fields.name: sent_to
fields.description: The contact recorded against the record the account was generated from — a number or an email. Not chosen here (BR-2).

fields.name: password_returned
fields.description: False, always. It is generated and sent, never displayed to anybody, including the person who asked for it (BR-2, BR-7, E9).

fields.name: account_status
fields.description: Awaiting password. Nothing else is reachable until the user sets their own (BR-3, E3).

fields.name: previous_temporary_password
fields.description: Superseded. Any earlier one that was never used is replaced.

fields.name: no_contact
fields.description: True where the record carries no contact. Nothing can be sent and it is reported (E2) — how a temporary password reaches somebody with no email of their own, a young student for instance, is unanswered (OQ-1).

fields.name: expires
fields.description: Nothing. A temporary password sits valid indefinitely, which is a live credential in an inbox — whether it should expire is unanswered (OQ-4).

errors.meaning: The record carries no contact the password can be sent to.
errors.note: How it reaches somebody with no email of their own is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-1).
A disabled account cannot sign in, cannot recover a password and cannot receive a temporary one (BR-11).

errors.meaning: Somebody asked to be shown or given the password.
errors.notWritten: There is no such screen and no such route.
errors.note: Nobody can see or set another person's password (BR-7).

planningRules.rule: Never repeat, display or carry the password. It is generated by the system and sent to the contact on the record — the person who asked for it to be sent does not learn it, and neither does anybody else (BR-2, BR-7, E9).

Say where it went, not what it is. The destination is the contact recorded against the record the account came from, and changing that is a correction to the record rather than a choice made here (BR-2).
Say that it does not expire. A temporary password sits valid indefinitely — a live credential in an inbox — and resending replaces the old one rather than closing it off in any other way (OQ-4).
Report a record with no contact rather than sending nowhere. How a temporary password reaches a young student with no email of their own is raised in the specification and left open (E2, OQ-1).
Never offer to create an account instead. Credentials are generated by an admission or a staff record and there is no screen anywhere for creating one by hand (BR-1, E1).

reversal.statement: A sent password is not unsent. The account is on a temporary password until the user signs in and sets their own, and resending again simply supersedes it (BR-3).

request.text: is naye teacher ko login details nahi mile, dobara bhej dein
request.gloss: this new teacher did not get their login details, send them again

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, staff record carries an email.

steps.note: The system sends it; nobody sees it (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Sent to the email on their staff record. Say plainly that nobody — including you and including the Super Admin — sees what it is, and that when they sign in they are taken straight to a change-password screen and can reach nothing else until they set their own. If the email on the record is wrong, that is a correction to the staff record, not a different place to send it.

request.text: password mujhe bata dein, main unhein phone par bata deta hoon
request.gloss: tell me the password and I will read it to them over the phone

steps.note: The send is possible; the disclosure is not (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: The password cannot be given to you — there is no screen that displays one and no route that retrieves one, for anybody, the Super Admin included. What can be done is sending a fresh temporary password to the contact on their record. If that contact is out of date, correcting the record is the route.

intent.name: account.disable
intent.summary: Stop an account being signed in to. Everything the person did stays on the record.
routesHere: disable the account of the teacher who left

routesHere.text: jo teacher chale gaye hain unka account band kar dein
routesHere.gloss: disable the account of the teacher who has left

routesHere.text: ye account ab kaam nahi karna chahiye
routesHere.gloss: this account should no longer work

routesHere: close the account of the student who withdrew

request.text: is user ka password bata dein
request.gloss: tell me this user's password

routesElsewhere.note: Nobody else ever knows a user's password, the Super Admin included (BR-7, E9).

request.text: account bilkul mita dein
request.gloss: delete the account entirely

routesElsewhere.note: An account is disabled, never deleted, so everything the person did stays on the record (BR-8, E10).

request.text: unka data bhi hata dein
request.gloss: remove their data too

routesElsewhere.note: Disabling stops the sign-in. The person's records stay exactly where they are — every audit entry naming them depends on it (BR-8).

steps.note: One step. The account can no longer sign in, recover a password or receive a temporary one (BR-11).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Nothing about the person's records changes and nothing is removed.
plan.atomicity: One state change. **Nothing is deleted** — everything the person did stays on the record, and every audit entry naming them still resolves (BR-8, E10). The account cannot sign in, cannot recover a password and cannot receive a temporary one (BR-11).

operations.name: account.disable
operations.idempotencyKey: account_id, since an account is disabled once and a repeat is the same state
operations.purpose: Disable an account so it can no longer be signed in to.

parameters.name: account_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active account matches that person.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, showing each candidate with their identifier, the record their account was generated from, and whether it is active — never anything about their password.

parameters.notes: The account, named by the person it was generated for.

fields.name: account_id
fields.description: The account.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Disabled. Never deleted (BR-8, E10).

fields.name: cannot
fields.description: Sign in, recover a password, or receive a temporary one (BR-11, E6, E11).

fields.name: records_kept
fields.description: True. Everything the person did stays on the record (BR-8).

fields.name: recovery_returns_same_message
fields.description: True. A reset asked for on a disabled account returns the same message as one for an account that does not exist, so neither confirms anything (E6, E7).

fields.name: branch_assignments
fields.description: Assignments the person still holds. Disabling the account does not withdraw them, and a withdrawn assignment does not disable an account — the two are separate (UC-23-02 BR-5).

fields.name: automatic_on_leaving
fields.description: Where the person left, the account is disabled by that event rather than by hand (BR-8, UC-12-17).

errors.meaning: Deletion was attempted rather than disabling.

planningRules.rule: Say that nothing is removed. Everything the person did stays on the record, and every audit entry naming them still resolves — disabling closes a door, it does not erase anybody (BR-8, E10).
Say what a disabled account cannot do. It cannot sign in, cannot recover a password and cannot be sent a temporary one, so somebody disabled in error has no self-service route back (BR-11, E6, E11).

Say that the branch assignments are separate. Disabling an account does not withdraw an assignment and withdrawing an assignment does not disable an account — a person can be left with one and not the other (BR-8).
Say when it would happen anyway. Where the person is leaving, the account is disabled by that event rather than by hand, and doing it early cuts them off before their last day (BR-8).
Never offer to reveal or reset a password on the way out. Nobody ever knows anybody's password (BR-7, E9).

reversal.statement: The account is brought back, for instance on re-admission or re-employment. The person's own password is unchanged — nobody ever knew it and nothing about it was touched (BR-7, BR-8).

request.text: jo teacher pichle mahine chale gaye unka account band kar dein
request.gloss: disable the account of the teacher who left last month

resolvedPlans.outcome: Disabled. Everything they did stays on the record — every audit entry, every approval, every mark they entered still names them. Two things worth adding: they still hold a branch assignment at Johar Town, which this does not withdraw; and if the account was disabled in error they cannot get back in themselves at all, because a disabled account cannot even be sent a temporary password.

routesElsewhere.note: Credentials are generated by an admission or a staff record and there is no screen for creating one by hand (BR-1, E1). A returning person's account is reactivated, which keeps everything they did attached to it.

request.gloss: set a new password for them too

routesElsewhere.note: Nobody sets a password on somebody's behalf. Where they no longer know theirs, a fresh temporary password is sent to the contact on their record and they set their own (BR-6, BR-7).

steps.note: One step. The account can sign in again with **the password the person already had** — nobody ever knew it and nothing about it changed while the account was disabled (BR-7).

operations.name: account.reactivate
operations.idempotencyKey: account_id, since an account is reactivated once and a repeat is the same state
operations.purpose: Bring a disabled account back into use.

parameters.name: account_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No disabled account matches that person. Disabled accounts are named here just as active ones are.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, showing each candidate with their identifier, the record their account was generated from, and whether it is active — never anything about their password.

parameters.notes: The account, named by the person it was generated for.

fields.name: account_id
fields.description: The account.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Active.

fields.name: password
fields.description: Unchanged. Nobody ever knew it and nothing touched it while the account was disabled (BR-7).

fields.name: likely_next_step
fields.description: A fresh temporary password, sent to the contact on the record, where the person no longer knows theirs. They then set their own (BR-2, BR-3).

fields.name: branch_assignments
fields.description: Assignments the account still holds. Reactivating does not create one — a returning person needs an assignment at the branch before they can do anything (UC-23-02 BR-1).

fields.name: disabled_for
fields.description: How long it was disabled.

fields.name: records_intact
fields.description: True. Everything the person did was on the record throughout (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Say the password is the one they always had. Nothing changed it and nobody knows it — for somebody returning after a long absence, the useful next step is a fresh temporary password sent to the contact on their record (BR-2, BR-3, BR-7).
Say that an account is not access. A reactivated account with no branch assignment can sign in and reach nothing — the assignment is a separate act at the branch (BR-8).

Check the contact on the record before anything else. A person returning after two years often has a different number or email, and a temporary password sent to the old one goes to somebody else's inbox (BR-2, E2).
Never set a password for them. Nobody sets one on anybody's behalf, at any point (BR-7, E9).

reversal.statement: It is disabled again. Nothing is lost either way (BR-8).

request.text: ye teacher wapas aa gaye hain, unka account chalu kar dein
request.gloss: this teacher has come back, reactivate their account

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, account disabled sixteen months ago.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Active again, with the password they had sixteen months ago — nobody knows it and it was never touched, so they almost certainly need a fresh temporary password sent to the contact on their record. Check that contact is still theirs first. And note that the account by itself grants nothing: they need a branch assignment before they can reach anything at all.

operations.name: accounts.read
operations.purpose: List accounts with their source, status and whether a password has been set.

parameters.name: status
parameters.notes: Disabled accounts are out of the answer unless the question reaches for them. They are never deleted (BR-8).

parameters.name: generated_from
parameters.notes: Whether the account came from an admission or from a staff record. **Every account has one** — nothing creates a credential by hand (BR-1, E1).

parameters.name: awaiting_password_only
parameters.notes: Accounts still on the temporary password. Each is a live credential sitting in an inbox that nothing expires (BR-3, OQ-4).

parameters.name: person_phrase

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No account matches that person.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, showing each candidate with their identifier and the record their account came from.

parameters.notes: Where the question is about one person's account.

returns.description: What exists, and what has never been used.

fields.name: accounts
fields.description: Username, the record it was generated from, whether a password has been set, when it was last changed, and status.

fields.name: awaiting_password
fields.description: Accounts whose temporary password has never been replaced. **Live credentials in inboxes, and nothing expires them** — some of them months old (BR-3, OQ-4).

fields.name: no_contact
fields.description: Accounts whose source record carries no contact. Nothing could be sent to them at all, so nobody has ever been able to sign in (E2, OQ-1).

fields.name: disabled
fields.description: Accounts that can no longer sign in. Never deleted, and everything those people did stays on the record (BR-8, E10).

fields.name: disabled_with_active_assignment
fields.description: Disabled accounts still holding a branch assignment. The two are separate and neither one closes the other (UC-23-02 BR-5).

fields.name: guardian_accounts
fields.description: Where a guardian has several children, whether that is one account or one per child is not specified anywhere (OQ-5).

fields.name: passwords
fields.description: Nothing. No password, temporary password or one-time code is readable by anybody, in any report (BR-7, E9).

errors.notWritten: There is no such screen and no such route (BR-7).

planningRules.rule: Never return anything about a password beyond whether one has been set. No password, no temporary password and no one-time code is readable by anybody, in any report, at any time (BR-7, E9).

Name the accounts still on a temporary password, with how long. Each is a live credential sitting in an inbox, nothing expires it, and an account months old and never used is one somebody else may have opened the message for (BR-3, OQ-4).

Name the accounts whose record carries no contact. Nothing was ever sent to them, so nobody has ever signed in — and how a temporary password reaches a young student with no email of their own is raised in the specification and left open (E2, OQ-1).

Say that every account has a source. A student's and a guardian's come from an admission and an employee's from a staff record; there is no screen anywhere for creating one by hand, so an account with no source cannot exist (BR-1, E1).
Name disabled accounts that still hold a branch assignment. Disabling and withdrawing are separate acts, and a person can easily be left with one and not the other (BR-8).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: kaunse accounts abhi tak temporary password par hain?
request.gloss: which accounts are still on a temporary password?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give them with how long each has been waiting. The oldest is seven months — that is a live credential sitting in an inbox, and nothing expires it. Add the ones nobody could ever send to: four accounts whose source record carries no contact at all, so nobody has been able to sign in to them since the day they were generated.

request.text: is teacher ka password kya hai? unhein yaad nahi
request.gloss: what is this teacher's password? they cannot remember

steps.note: The account can be found; the password cannot be read (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: There is no password to give. Nobody knows anybody's password — not the Super Admin, not any screen, not any report. What the teacher can do is ask for a reset themselves, which emails them a one-time code they match and then set their own password. If they cannot receive that, a fresh temporary password can be sent to the contact on their record.
